Bajaj Finance Builds 328-Member AI Team, Targets Expansion Of AI Agents

Bajaj Finance has built a 328-member team dedicated to artificial intelligence (AI) as it expands automation across its business, with AI bots now handling around 75 per cent of customer queries received through its do-it-yourself service channels.
The company’s FinAI unit is leading the initiative, with management outlining plans to extend AI applications beyond customer-facing services to wider enterprise operations.

During its Q2 FY27 earnings call, management said Bajaj Finance currently has around 129 AI agents and 65 agentic applications. The company aims to increase these numbers to approximately 600 AI agents and 118 agentic applications during the year.
From Customer Service To Enterprise Operations

AI bots currently handle about three-fourths of the queries received through the company’s self-service channels, enabling routine customer interactions to be addressed with less human intervention.The next phase of the strategy is expected to extend AI adoption across the organisation. Management said FinAI is moving towards enterprise-wide transformation, with applications intended to support both employees and customers.

The expansion reflects a broader shift in financial services, from deploying chatbots for routine interactions to developing AI systems capable of undertaking more complex, multi-step tasks across business functions.
Growing Demand For Specialised AI Talent

The expansion of Bajaj Finance’s dedicated AI team also highlights the workforce requirements accompanying automation. Financial institutions need specialised talent to develop, deploy and manage AI systems even as these technologies take over parts of existing workflows.The planned increase in AI agents and agentic applications will indicate how quickly the company moves from task-level automation towards wider process transformation.

However, Bajaj Finance has not disclosed whether increased AI adoption has led to a reduction in employee numbers, changes in specific job roles or a lower requirement for customer-service staff. The 328-member FinAI team should therefore be viewed as a measure of the company’s dedicated AI capability, rather than a direct indicator of jobs created or displaced by automation.
